hints: Use inclusion-exclusion on forbidden adjacent pairs (1,2), (2,3), and so on.
Selected forbidden pairs form disjoint runs along the number line.
Each run becomes one block that can be oriented in two ways.
analogy: Glue chosen neighboring numbers together into runs, count the resulting block arrangements, and alternate signs.
example: For n=3, every permutation contains either adjacent 1 and 2 or adjacent 2 and 3, so the answer is 0.
algorithm: For each number j of selected forbidden edges and c of nonempty runs of selected edges in the path of n numbers, count edge selections as C(j-1,c-1)*C(n-j,c), for j>0. These edges form c nontrivial blocks and n-j total blocks. Their permutations and orientations contribute (n-j)!*2^c. Sum (-1)^j times this quantity over j and c modulo 1000000007; include j=0 as n!. Precompute factorials and binomial coefficients.
correctness: Inclusion-exclusion removes permutations containing any forbidden pair. Every chosen set of j edges decomposes uniquely into c runs. Compressing each run leaves n-j blocks; each nontrivial run has exactly two valid orientations. The binomial formula selects positive run lengths and places the separated runs among the n-1 path edges.
complexity: For n numbers, evaluating all j,c pairs takes O(n^2) time and O(n^2) space with a binomial table, or O(n) space with factorials and inverse factorials.
